overview.what_it_does: Dixon Technologies is India's largest homegrown electronics contract manufacturer — it builds finished electronic products in its own Indian factories for other companies' brands rather than selling under its own name. Its customers are smartphone brands (including a large U.S. brand), telecom and broadband operators, PC brands like HP, ASUS and Lenovo, and TV, refrigerator, washing-machine and lighting brands; it works both as a pure assembler (EMS, where the brand hands over the design) and as an ODM, where Dixon designs the product itself and earns a better margin. Money is made on volume assembly at thin margins — FY26 revenue of INR48,893 crores produced EBITDA of INR1,887 crores (roughly 4%) and PAT of INR845 crores — with the business run on negative working capital (negative 8 days) and very high return ratios (ROCE 44.8%, ROE 28.1%). Manufacturing is entirely India-based (Noida, Greater Noida, Chennai, Tirupati), mostly for the domestic market with exports beginning in lighting, telecom radios, low-cost refrigerators and feature phones for Africa, and the current strategy is to move down into making the components it currently buys — display modules, camera modules, enclosures, batteries — largely through joint ventures with foreign partners.

parts.name: Mobile and other EMS
parts.what: Assembles smartphones, feature phones, hearables and wearables for multiple brands and is by far the dominant business — INR9,485 crores of the INR10,520 crores Q4 FY26 revenue, though it has recently been hurt by sharply rising memory-chip prices and softer demand.

parts.name: Telecom and Networking products
parts.what: Makes 5G fixed-wireless-access devices, IPTV set-top boxes and, newly, complex backhaul microwave radios; it grew over 250% year-on-year in Q1 FY26 to INR1,410 crores in the quarter and management expects high double-digit growth again this fiscal.

parts.name: IT hardware products
parts.what: Builds laptops, all-in-one PCs, tablets and now desktops at a dedicated Chennai plant for HP, ASUS and Lenovo, including a 60:40 joint venture with Taiwan's Inventec; still small (INR331 crores in Q2 FY26) but management guides to 3x revenue growth this year and is exploring servers and data-centre hardware.

parts.name: Consumer electronics (LED TVs and refrigerators)
parts.what: Makes LED TVs — increasingly premium mini-LED and large-screen sets, with about 65% of volumes on its own ODM designs — plus direct-cool refrigerators, mini bars and soon deep freezers and side-by-side models; quarterly revenue runs roughly INR570–960 crores at around 4–6% operating margin.

parts.name: Home appliances
parts.what: Designs and manufactures washing machines end-to-end (semi-automatic, and front-load from Q2 FY27) plus robotic vacuum cleaners for Eureka Forbes; small at about INR330–430 crores a quarter but the most profitable segment at roughly 11.5% operating margin.

parts.name: Lighting
parts.what: Makes LED lighting products, run since August 2025 through Lightanium Technologies, a 50:50 joint venture with Signify (the Philips brand), adding premium indoor and professional lighting and early export pilot orders to large U.S. and German retail chains; the smallest segment at INR188 crores in Q1 FY26.

parts.name: Components / backward integration
parts.what: A newly built layer making the parts Dixon used to buy — display modules (74:26 JV with HKC), camera and fingerprint modules (51%-owned Q Tech India, scaling from 40–70 million to 180–200 million units), enclosures, lithium-ion batteries, optical transceivers and SSDs — backed by roughly INR3,000 crores of committed investment and government ECMS incentives, and pitched as the main source of future margin expansion.
